title: Canonical qcqs strict-local comparison for module coefficients
statement: Let Λ be a commutative coefficient ring, f:X→Y a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], s:Spec Ω→Y a geometric point with Ω algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], and F a sheaf of Λ-modules on X_et [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Write R=O^sh_(Y,s) and ρ:Spec R→Y for the affine pointed-neighbourhood colimit and its structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit; def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], Z=X×_Y Spec R, p:Z→X, H=p⁻¹F. For each small-model affine pointed representative (V,v), let c_V:Spec R→V be the canonical limit leg followed by Spec Γ(V,⊤)≅V. The map Z→V×_Y X has components (h c_V,p), where h:Z→Spec R. Its graph gives the terminal-neighbourhood morphism δ_V from Z to p⁻¹(V×_Y X). Define r_V:F(V×_Y X)→Γ(Z,H) to be the p-adjunction unit at V×_Y X, restriction along δ_V, and the inverse terminal-section identification. This is implemented by qcqsStrictLocalNeighbourhoodSection and qcqsStrictLocalSectionRestriction, using pullback symmetry to match the library's reversed orientation. There is an isomorphism e:(f_*F)_s≅Γ(Z,H) such that germ_(V,v) followed by e.hom equals r_V for every affine pointed representative. The predicate IsQcqsStrictLocalModuleComparison is exactly these equations. Stalks and germs use pointSmallEtale.sheafFiber and toPresheafFiber [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. This asserts continuity and its representative formula; it says nothing about exchange or restriction to a geometric fibre.

proof.text: For the transported small-model graph maps, prove refinement compatibility directly inside the cocone construction. Identify base-change cone legs by their two projections, apply cone naturality, and use pullback extensionality for graph compatibility. Naturality of the module adjunction unit and contravariant functoriality then make the specified linear restrictions a cocone. This retains the original small-model definitions and all germ equations.

Initiality of the affine pointed-neighbourhood inclusion makes the whiskered module stalk cocone a colimit. Its desc to the restriction cocone constructs a linear map; the colimit fac equation gives every required germ equation.

Base change Spec.map of the inverse canonical small/full ring-colimit isomorphism and compose with pullback symmetry. This gives an isomorphism over X between the small-model target scheme and the full strict localization; its composite with every full-model leg equals the symmetry followed by the small-model leg, by definition.

Apply exists_moduleSectionsIsoTransport to this isomorphism over X. It gives a bijection from module global sections to the full-model set terminal sections and the formula for transported units and graphs. The forgetful functor preserves the filtered colimit defining the stalk, so sheafFiberCompIso gives the source bijection compatibly with germs.

Conjugate the constructed linear map by these bijections. Its cocone fac equations, the coefficient-forgetting germ identity and the transported graph formula identify it with the unique official set comparison. That comparison is bijective. Cancel the source and target bijections and use ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective, then asIso. This proves invertibility inside the construction; the separate small-model restriction-isomorphism declaration is no longer needed.

Use the transported small-model leg and its two projection identities from [def-weil-pbc-small-strict-local-section-maps] in place of unfolding the retired duplicate definition. The representative restriction formula and all existing mathematical hypotheses remain unchanged.
